title: Anticuchos
subtitle: Peruvian grilled beef heart skewers with aji panca marinade
excerpt: Anticuchos are Peruvian beef heart skewers marinated in aji panca paste, garlic, cumin and vinegar. The meat is threaded onto skewers and grilled over high heat until charred and tender. They are sold as street food across Peru and are one of the country's most iconic dishes.
sourceNotes: Anticuchos were eaten by the Incas before Spanish colonisation. During the colonial era, enslaved Africans in Lima developed the dish using offal, marinating beef heart in vinegar, spices and chilli to make it tender and flavourful. Today anticuchos are sold by street vendors throughout Peru, especially in Lima.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the beef heart overnight in the fridge for a deeper flavour.

glossaryTerms.definition: A dark red Peruvian dried chilli with a deep, smoky flavour and low to moderate heat. It is the key ingredient in anticuchos and gives them their distinctive colour and taste.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 as a starter and takes 35 minutes of active work plus at least 4 hours of marinating time. The 600g of beef heart is cut into 3cm cubes and marinated in a paste of
, vinegar, cumin and garlic before being threaded onto skewers and cooked over very high heat.

Beef heart is a lean muscle with a firm texture. It benefits from both a long marinade and fast, fierce cooking. Do not cook it slowly or it will toughen. Soak wooden skewers in water for at least 30 minutes before use to prevent scorching. A ridged grill pan works well if you do not have an outdoor grill.
Soak wooden skewers in cold water for at least 30 minutes.
Clean 600g beef heart by removing any visible fat, sinew and white membrane. Cut the meat into 3cm cubes.
Thread 3 to 4 pieces of heart onto each skewer. Leave a small gap between pieces so heat reaches the sides. Brush generously with the marinade.
Add the beef heart cubes to the marinade and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
When ready to cook, thread 4 to 5 pieces of beef heart onto each skewer. Allow a little space between each piece so the heat circulates.

Heat a ridged grill pan over the highest heat until smoking. Brush with the remaining tablespoon of oil. Cook the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side, turning once, until charred on the outside and still slightly pink in the centre.
Remove from the heat and rest for 2 minutes. Serve with fresh coriander and lime wedges.

attrs.symptom: Beef heart is tough and chewy
attrs.cause: The heat was too low or the meat was cooked for too long
attrs.fix: Use the highest heat available and cook quickly. Beef heart is at its best when still slightly pink inside, around 3 to 4 minutes per side.

attrs.symptom: Marinade does not stick to the meat
attrs.cause: The meat was wet when added to the marinade
attrs.fix: Pat the beef heart dry with kitchen paper before adding it to the marinade so the paste can adhere properly.

attrs.symptom: Skewers are burning before the meat is cooked
attrs.cause: Wooden skewers were not soaked long enough
attrs.fix: Soak skewers in cold water for at least 30 minutes, or use metal skewers if available.

content.text: Anticuchos are classic Lima street food, sold from carts and small stalls in the evening. The smell of charring beef heart and chilli smoke is one of the defining street aromas of the city. They are also served in traditional restaurants across Peru.
